chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a Muslim man who was in the land of shirk and was killed by the Muslims, then the Imam later came to know of him, so he said:
“He should free in his place a believing slave, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
‘But if he belonged to a people hostile to you, and he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave [is required].’

key_terms.أَرْضِ ٱلشِّرْكِ: the land of polytheism or hostile non-Muslim territory
key_terms.رَقَبَةً مُؤْمِنَةً: a believing slave to be freed as expiation
key_terms.فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ: the obligation of freeing a believing slave
key_terms.قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَكُمْ: a people who are hostile to you
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامُ: the Imam, the divinely guided authority who issues the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation if Muslims mistakenly kill a believer living in enemy territory?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the case of a Muslim living in enemy territory who is killed by Muslims. The Imam عليه السلام rules that a believing slave must be freed as expiation, citing the Qur'anic ruling in Surah al-Nisāʾ 4:92 as the basis for this judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5325 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from some of his companions from Abu Abdullah (as)
regarding a Muslim man who was in the land of the disbelievers and was mistakenly killed by the Muslims. Later, the Imam became aware of it.
Imam (as) said: "A believing slave must be freed in his place, and this is in accordance with the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic:
'But if he belonged to a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave [is required]'
